page.layout: One printed page with a single column of running text, justified. No marginal notes are printed. Catchword at the lower right below the last line. Edge of the neighbouring page and show-through along the margins are not transcribed.

main_text.p: doniæ praefectus Thebanos tum forte judiciis suis offenderat graviter. At Romæ, auditis illic legatis, qui domum jam redierant, & allatis quoque à Metello literis, autoribus potissimū iis, qui belli causam modò quærebant, & occasiones inchoandi ejus desiderabant, festinantius omnino quàm par erat, bellum in Achæos est decretum, & L. Mummius consul tum creatus, ad id gerendum ire jussus. Is quanta potuit festinatione cum copiis necessariis in Græciam contendit, ne victoriæ palmam Metellus præriperet. Metellus contra, qui arma jam ceperat, cognita re de Mummio, & ipse quoque acceleravit, ut ante ejus adventum bello finem imponeret. Itaque per nuncios celeres edixit Achæis, ut Lacedæmonem, & civitates alias, quæ partium Romanarum esse mallent, missas facerent: id si facerent, promisit, sese obliteratis prioribus offensis pristinæ Romanorum gratiæ eos esse restituturum.
Simul vero per Macedoniam exercitu ducto in hostes contendit.
At Critolaus rejecta omni de pace oratione cum Achæorum & sociorum copiis in Thessaliam progressus præsidium validum Thebanorum Heraclæ in fide nutanti impofuit: ipse audito Metelli adventu,

page.notes: The word "contra," carries a small red reference mark that could not be identified; no matching note is printed. A dot or mark stands before "Mummio" in "de Mummio"; uncertain. Faint marks at the foot below the catchword (near "defer-") are not legible and were left out. Printed "inchoandi" and "ducto" show ligature/long-letter forms rendered as plain text. Paragraph breaks were judged from line endings: the lines ending "restituturum." and "contendit." stop well short of the margin.
